details.description: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct is a 7.61-billion-parameter (6.53B non-embedding) code-focused chat model from Alibaba's Qwen team, released November 12, 2024 as part of the Qwen2.5-Coder family, the successor to CodeQwen. Qwen's model card states it was trained on 5.5 trillion tokens of source code, text-code grounding data, and synthetic data, and is instruction-tuned for code generation, code reasoning, and code repair while retaining general math and reasoning ability for uses such as code agents. Its published configuration gives a native 32,768-token context window, matching this catalog's limits. As of this research, Qwen's GitHub repository for the Qwen2.5-Coder project now redirects to the newer Qwen3-Coder project, though the Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct weights and model card remain published without an explicit deprecation notice.
advantages: Trained on 5.5 trillion tokens of source code, text-code grounding data, and synthetic data, per Qwen's model card.
Retains general math and reasoning competencies alongside coding skill, useful for applications such as code agents, per Qwen's model card.
Native context window of 32,768 tokens, extendable up to 131,072 tokens using YaRN scaling, per Qwen's model card.
disadvantages: Qwen's GitHub repository for the Qwen2.5-Coder project now redirects to the newer Qwen3-Coder repository, indicating Qwen's coding-model development has moved to that newer line.
Qwen's model card notes that vLLM's YaRN implementation for extending context beyond 32,768 tokens only supports static scaling factors, which can affect performance on shorter texts once enabled.
use_cases: Code agent applications that combine coding with general reasoning

sources.title: QwenLM/Qwen2.5-Coder now redirects to QwenLM/Qwen3-Coder · GitHub

notes: Catalog's max_input_tokens/max_output_tokens (32,768) match the model's published config.json max_position_embeddings exactly, so no conflict. No numeric coding-benchmark scores (HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, etc.) specific to the 7B-Instruct size were found in text form on Qwen's model card or blog post (the blog's per-size benchmark tables are embedded as images), so evaluations was left empty rather than guessed. Qwen's GitHub org page for 'QwenLM/Qwen2.5-Coder' now resolves to the 'QwenLM/Qwen3-Coder' repository (confirmed by fetching it and checking the resolved title/URL), so github_url was left null since that repo no longer represents this specific 2.5-generation model; this supersession signal is also reflected in the description and disadvantages.
